spec_cite: docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §7.1 (reserved-flag rule: sender MUST zero bits 2–31, receiver MUST ignore them)
docs/wire-protocol-v2/spec.md §7.5 (any of flag bits 2–31 set: never malformed, processed exactly as if zero)
description: A datagram with the highest reserved flag bit set (bit 31, 0x80000000) is processed normally — reserved bits are IGNORED, never rejected and never treated as malformed, at the top of the reserved range exactly as within it.
preconditions: The reserved-bit rule is normative (spec §7.1, §7.5): the sender MUST zero bits 2–31; the receiver MUST ignore them and MUST NOT treat them as malformed. This vector pins the receiver's tolerance at bit 31; it is not a license for a sender to set the bit.

steps.note: flags = 0x80000000: the highest reserved bit (bit 31) set; the sender MUST zero bits 2–31 and the receiver MUST ignore them — processed exactly as if flags were 0.

assertions: The datagram is processed exactly as if flags were 0: decoded, deduped, buffered (§7.5) — bit 31 is as ignorable as bit 2 (see media.flags-reserved-ignored).
The receiver MUST NOT treat any of bits 2–31 as malformed; zeroing them is the sender's obligation (spec §7.1, §7.5).
A future revision may promote specific reserved bits to mandatory — until then receivers MUST ignore them (§7.1).
